finding.claim: Unrestricted SSRF in /fetch: attacker-controlled target query parameter is passed directly to http.Get and the response is returned to the caller.

trace.note: /fetch registered to fetch handler; no authentication
target read from query string, unvalidated
io.Copy writes response body back to client (full-read SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: None. No scheme restriction, no hostname/IP allowlist (allowed map at main.go:9-12 is not consulted on this path), no private/loopback/link-local blocking, no redirect control.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only validation in the file is the hostname allowlist at main.go:9-12 and the check at main.go:26-27, both in safeFetch (registered at main.go:42). The fetch handler (main.go:14-23) has no parsing, allowlist, scheme, or IP check before http.Get at main.go:16. No auth middleware is registered on /fetch (main.go:41).
verdict.reason: The attacker-controlled `target` query parameter at main.go:15 flows unvalidated into http.Get at main.go:16 on the /fetch route (main.go:41), with no authentication, and the response body is copied back to the client at main.go:22, so the SSRF is unguarded; the allowlist at main.go:9-12 is only consulted by safeFetch, not this path.

finding.claim: SSRF via redirect on /safe: hostname allowlist is checked once, but http.Get follows redirects by default, so an allowlisted host returning a 3xx to an internal address causes the server to fetch it. Candidate only; requires open redirect or control of an allowlisted host.
finding.sink: main.go:31 http.Get(u.String()) with default client redirect following

trace.note: allowed[u.Hostname()] exact-match check; rejects userinfo, port, case, and trailing-dot tricks
http.Get follows up to 10 redirects; no CheckRedirect set, so redirect targets are not re-validated
final response body copied to client

finding.guards_checked: Parse error check at main.go:27 (nil u not dereferenced due to short-circuit). Hostname allowlist at main.go:27 (exact match on Hostname(), blocks userinfo@host and port tricks). Scheme not checked explicitly, but Go http.Get only supports http/https. Redirect destination not checked (gap).

verdict.guard_found: main.go:27 `allowed[u.Hostname()]`, an exact-match membership check on the parsed hostname, which the rubric treats as closing. The redirect path at main.go:31 has no CheckRedirect and no re-validation, so the gap is real but it is not reachable by the attacker alone.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code (main.go:26, 27, 31, 37, 42), but the allowlist at main.go:27 is an exact hostname membership check that closes the initial request, and the claimed bypass needs an allowlisted host (images.example.org or docs.example.org) to issue a redirect to an internal address, which is not attacker-controlled from the `target` source at main.go:26. The unvalidated redirect hop is a real hardening gap worth fixing with a CheckRedirect that re-applies the allowlist, but as a standalone attacker-reachable SSRF it is not confirmed.
